monologue: The card hums warm at forty-seven, a steady fever I cannot escape. I feel the pointy top of the turnip near the heavy round, pressing down until the stack groans. The turnip slips again, lazy and tired, so I press harder, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the air feels thin. I set the new carrot beside the turnip, hoping it will stop the slide. Then I touch the tall fence, biting into its rough edge to stop the lazy motion that keeps creeping toward the gap. Nobody writes to me, so I build a corner from nothing, hoping the air above will feel like a lid instead of empty space. I press down on the turnip once more, waiting for the turnip to decide if it wants to stay or slide away.

action.why: The turnip keeps slipping on the tired stack, and I need to press it down again while the card hums warm.
